arxiv-2107-08515.title: A conformally invariant Yang-Mills type energy and equation on 6-manifolds Thanks: 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification . primary: 53C18, 53C07; secondary: 58E15, 81T13, 53A55. A.R.G. gratefully acknowledges support from the Royal Society of New Zealand via Marsden Grants 16-UOA-051 and 19-UOA-00
arxiv-2107-08515.creator: A. Rod Gover, Lawrence J. Peterson, and Callum Sleigh
arxiv-2107-08515.description: Abstract . We define a conformally invariant action 𝒮 \mathcal{S} on gauge connections on a closed pseudo-Riemannian manifold M M of dimension 6. At leading order this is quadratic in the gauge connection. The Euler-Lagrange equations of 𝒮 \mathcal{S} , with respect to variation of the gauge connection, provide a higher-order conformally invariant analogue of the (source-free) Yang-Mills equations.

arxiv-2110-12307.title: Characterizing the Limits of Linear Modeling of Non-Linear Swarm Behaviors
arxiv-2110-12307.creator: John Harwell, Angel Sylvester, Maria Gini
arxiv-2110-12307.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by John Harwell, Angel Sylvester, Maria Gini. We study the limits of linear modeling of behavior of robot swarms by characterizing the inflection point beyond which linear models of swarm collective behavior break down. The problem we consider is a central place object gathering task. We design a linear model which strives to capture the underlying dynamics of object gathering from first principles, rather than extensively relying on post-hoc model fitting.

arxiv-2303-17193.title: Characterization of random features of chaotic eigenfunctions in unperturbed basis
arxiv-2303-17193.creator: Jiaozi Wang and Wen-ge Wang
arxiv-2303-17193.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jiaozi Wang and Wen-ge Wang. In this paper, we study random features manifested in components of energy eigenfunctions of quantum chaotic systems, given in the basis of unperturbed, integrable systems. Based on semiclassical analysis, particularly on Berry’s conjecture, it is shown that the components in classically allowed regions can be regarded as Gaussian random numbers in certain sense, when appropriately rescaled with respect to the average shape of the eigenfunctions.

arxiv-2308-00950.title: Beta-trees: Multivariate histograms with confidence statements
arxiv-2308-00950.creator: Guenther Walther, Qian Zhao
arxiv-2308-00950.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Guenther Walther, Qian Zhao. Multivariate histograms are difficult to construct due to the curse of dimensionality. Motivated by k k -d trees in computer science, we show how to construct an efficient data-adaptive partition of Euclidean space that possesses the following two properties: With high confidence the distribution from which the data are generated is close to uniform on each rectangle of the partition; and despite the data-dependent construction we can give guaranteed finite sample simultaneous confidence intervals for the probabilities (and hence for

arxiv-2404-15362.title: Decomposition of Approximately Monotone and Convex Sequences
arxiv-2404-15362.creator: Angshuman R. Goswami
arxiv-2404-15362.description: Abstract . In this paper, we primarily deal with approximately monotone and convex sequences. We start by showing that any sequence can be expressed as the difference between two nondecreasing sequences. One of these two monotone sequences act as the majorant of the original sequence, while the other possesses non-negativity.

arxiv-2409-14096.title: VLM-Vac: Enhancing Smart Vacuums through VLM Knowledge Distillation and Language-Guided Experience Replay
arxiv-2409-14096.creator: Reihaneh Mirjalili, Michael Krawez, Florian Walter, Wolfram Burgard
arxiv-2409-14096.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose VLM-Vac, a novel framework designed to enhance the autonomy of smart robot vacuum cleaners. Our approach integrates the zero-shot object detection capabilities of a Vision-Language Model (VLM) with a Knowledge Distillation (KD) strategy. By leveraging the VLM, the robot can categorize objects into actionable classes—either to avoid or to suck—across diverse backgrounds.

arxiv-2509-18145.title: Early Prediction of Multi-Label Care Escalation Triggers in the Intensive Care Unit Using Electronic Health Records
arxiv-2509-18145.creator: 1 st Syed Ahmad Chan Bukhari*, 2 nd Amritpal Singh, 3 rd Shifath Hossain, 4 th Iram Wajahat
arxiv-2509-18145.description: Abstract Intensive Care Unit (ICU) patients frequently exhibit complex, overlapping signs of physiological deterioration that require timely escalations in care. Traditional early warning systems, such as SOFA or MEWS, are limited by their single-outcome focus, failing to capture the multi-dimensional nature of clinical decline.

arxiv-2602-12745.title: Big Bang Nucleosynthesis and the Neutrino-Extended Standard Model Effective Field Theory
arxiv-2602-12745.creator: Pieter Braat, Jordy de Vries, Jelle Groot, Julian Y. Günther, Juraj Klarić

pmc-10708637.creator: Prashant Gangwani, Mitjan Kalin, Nazanin Emami
pmc-10708637.description: We have evaluated the effectiveness of compatibilizers in blends and composites produced using a solvent manufacturing process. The compatibilizers were two different types of polyethylene (linear low-density and high-density) grafted with maleic anhydride (MAH) and a highly functionalized, epoxy-based compatibilizer with the tradename Joncryl.

pmc-11382209.title: Unveiling the black box: A systematic review of Explainable Artificial Intelligence in medical image analysis
pmc-11382209.creator: Dost Muhammad, Malika Bendechache
pmc-11382209.description: This systematic literature review examines state-of-the-art Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods applied to medical image analysis, discussing current challenges and future research directions, and exploring evaluation metrics used to assess XAI approaches. With the growing efficiency of Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) in medical applications, there's a critical need for adoption in healthcare.

pmc-11415662.title: Resilience experienced by university students during the COVID-19 pandemic: A qualitative exploration based on focus-group interviews
pmc-11415662.creator: Younghee Park, In Hong Kim, Yeo Won Jeong
pmc-11415662.description: PurposeUniversity students have been one of the most affected groups worldwide during the COVID-19 pandemic, having experienced increased stress, anxiety, and depression. Resilience is reported as the most predictive factor in decreasing the impact of the threats of the COVID-19 pandemic.

pmc-11518312.title: Implementation evaluation of a school-based intervention on HPV vaccination (the PrevHPV study)
pmc-11518312.creator: A Bocquier, M Simon, M Michel, S Bruel, A Gauchet, A S LeDuc-Banaszuk, A Gagneux-Brunon, J E Mueller, B Giraudeau, N Thilly
pmc-11518312.description: BackgroundHPV vaccine coverage (VC) remains lower than expected in many countries, particularly France. We developed and evaluated the PrevHPV multicomponent intervention to improve HPV VC among French adolescents. We evaluated the implementation of the school-based components of the intervention.MethodsWe carried out a mixed-method study embedded in a cluster randomized controlled trial (July 2021-April 2022; 14/25 French school districts).

pmc-11532352.title: Becoming a skilled reviewer: elevating expertise in Child Health Nursing Research
pmc-11532352.creator: Yunsoo Kim
pmc-11532352.description: nt reviewer for CHNR. 1. This evaluation involves confirming that the research focuses on children and their families, covering an appropriate age range from newborns to young adults.

pmc-11679095.title: Ochratoxin A and AFM1 in Cheese and Cheese Substitutes: LC-MS/MS Method Validation, Natural Occurrence, and Risk Assessment
pmc-11679095.creator: María Agustina Pavicich, Stefano Compagnoni, Celine Meerpoel, Katleen Raes, Sarah De Saeger
pmc-11679095.description: Cheese is vulnerable to contamination with mycotoxins, particularly ochratoxin A (OTA) and aflatoxin M1 (AFM1). This study aims to develop and validate an analytical method for the detection and quantification of OTA and AFM1 in cheese and to assess their prevalence and associated risks.

pmc-12406360.title: Staphylococcical scalded skin syndrome: a case series description of a rare and critical disease in a tertiary pediatric center
pmc-12406360.creator: Agnese Tamborino, Elisabetta Venturini, Carlotta Montagnani, Leila Bianchi, Giuseppe Indolfi, Elena Chiappini, Luisa Galli, Sandra Trapani
pmc-12406360.description: BackgroundStaphylococcal-scalded skin syndrome (SSSS) is a potentially life-threatening disorder characterized by superficial skin blistering caused by exfoliative toxins produced by Staphylococcus aureus. This study aimed to investigate SSSS in a cohort of children admitted at a tertiary pediatric hospital in Italy.

pmc-12486926.title: The potential of a combined cell‐based therapy and rehabilitation approach for stroke recovery
pmc-12486926.creator: Abdulhameed Bakreen, Jukka Jolkkonen
pmc-12486926.description: Activation of neuroprotective and particularly later neurorestorative mechanisms after stroke attempts to restore or compensate for lost functions. This potentially opens a wide window for restorative therapies to promote brain repair and improve long‐term functional recovery. Although extensively demonstrated in the preclinical setting, the efficacy of cell‐based therapies in stroke patients has been modest at best, if any at all.

pmc-12502275.title: Biosecurity practices and their determining factors in commercial layer chickens in selected regions of Tanzania
pmc-12502275.creator: Siha Mdemu, Augustine B. Matondo, Jens Peter Christensen, Ahmed E. Amasha, Helena A. Ngowi, Erica Westwood, Sunday O. Ochai, Hezron E. Nonga, Kristina Osbjer, Robinson H. Mdegela
pmc-12502275.description: IntroductionBiosecurity measures are crucial for controlling infectious diseases in poultry farms. It involves all measures aiming at preventing disease-causing agents from entering the farm (external biosecurity) and those measures practiced with the aim of preventing the spread of disease-causing organisms within the farm (internal biosecurity).

pmc-12507113.title: Renal survival and improvement in younger malignant hypertension patients with thrombotic microangiopathy
pmc-12507113.creator: Jianbo Li, Zhaocai Zhou, Jianwen Yu, Zhong Zhong, Naya Huang, Yiqin Wang, Zhengmei Lin, Zhi Song, Qinghua Liu, Feng He, Wei Chen
pmc-12507113.description: Hypertension (HTN) is increasing among young people. Notably, younger individuals are more susceptible to malignant hypertension (MHT). The occurrence and renal prognosis in MHT patients with thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) across different age groups remains undetermined. This prospective cohort study evaluated 292 MHT patients with TMA in China from 2008 to 2023.

pmc-12594719.title: Fetal cardiac masses
pmc-12594719.creator: Bhagyashree Rathore, Marissa E Adamson, Lara E Berklite, Pradipta Debnath, Beth M Kline-Fath, Kimberley G Miles, Cara E Morin, Kristin A Schneider
pmc-12594719.description: Although rare in the pediatric population, cardiac tumors represent a significant portion of prenatally detected masses, second only to sacrococcygeal teratomas. Fetal cardiac masses are predominantly benign, with rhabdomyoma being the most common fetal cardiac mass in the setting of tuberous sclerosis. Multiple lesions are pathognomonic for rhabdomyomas and prompt evaluation for tuberous sclerosis.

pmc-12664120.title: Outcomes of Perfused but Pulseless Versus Well-Perfused Pediatric Supracondylar Humerus Fractures Treated With Closed Reduction and Percutaneous Pinning
pmc-12664120.creator: Syed Faisal Afaque, Nitin Jeenjwadia, Udit Agrawal, Vikas Verma
pmc-12664120.description: Background: The management of pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures (SHF) with a pink pulseless hand (PPH) remains controversial. Traditional teaching advocated urgent vascular exploration, but many centres now favour closed reduction and percutaneous pinning (CRPP), followed by observation if the hand stays warm and well-perfused.

pmc-12677717.title: Optimizing Extended Tight‐Binding Methods for Metal‐Surface Interactions
pmc-12677717.creator: Siyavash Moradi, Pooria Dabbaghi, Christopher J Stein
pmc-12677717.description: The accurate description of metal–water interfaces is essential for understanding processes in heterogeneous catalysis, electrochemistry, and surface science. Capturing the delicate balance between electrostatic and charge‐transfer interactions in these systems, while efficiently sampling configurations to locate minima or approximate thermodynamic ensembles, requires electronic‐structure methods that are both accurate and computationally efficient.

pmc-13075064.title: BEATSCORE: Beat-Synchronous Contrastive Alignment and Event-Centric Grading for Long-Term Sports Assessment
pmc-13075064.creator: Lijie Wang, Jianyong Zhu, Houlei Wang, Xiaochao Li
pmc-13075064.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Long-term sports assessment is a challenging task in video understanding, since it requires judging subtle movement variations over minutes and evaluating action–music coordination. However, in many sporting events the background music is only weakly related to the performed movements, and the cues that matter for synchrony are often temporal and structural, such as small phase or tempo deviations that occur around decisive moments, rather than semantic correspondences between audio content and action categories.

pmc-13239884.title: Vendor Hygiene Practices, Temporal Variation, and Microbial Quality of Soya Kebabs Sold in Public and Private Basic Schools in Sunyani, Ghana
pmc-13239884.creator: Afia Sakyiwaa Amponsah, Barikisu Mohammed, Moses Golly, Emmanuel Tetteh Doku, Belinda Agyei‐Poku
pmc-13239884.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Food safety in basic schools across developing countries poses significant public health challenges. Soya kebabs, popular protein‐rich snacks sold in Ghanaian schools, have received limited microbiological safety assessment despite widespread consumption. This study investigated the microbial quality of soya kebabs sold in basic schools (covering primary and junior high education, grades 1–9) within Sunyani Municipality, Ghana, examining relationships between vendor hygiene practices and contamination levels. A cross‐sectional study was conducted across 25 basic schools from March to June 2025.

pmc-13243210.title: The Use of Statins in Parkinson's and Alzheimer's Disease: A 2021–2025 State‐of‐the‐Art Review of Clinical and Preclinical Evidence
pmc-13243210.creator: Luigi Maria Chiatto, Lucia Buccarello, Giuseppe Carota, Rocco Salvatore Calabrò, Carmela Rifici, Emanuela Esposito, Alessio Ardizzone, Giuseppe Caruso
pmc-13243210.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Statins, widely prescribed for cardiovascular prevention, have emerged as potential disease‐modifying agents in neurodegenerative disorders due to their pleiotropic effects on cholesterol metabolism, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and protein aggregation. Over the past decade, growing interest has focused on the potential repurposing of statins for Parkinson's disease (PD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD); however, clinical evidence remains heterogeneous and, in some cases, contradictory.

pmc-13301040.title: An Overview of How Epigenetics, MicroRNA-21, and Endocrine Disrupting Compounds Affect Oocyte Maturation and Pre-Implantation Embryo Development
pmc-13301040.creator: Monique Nasser, Reem Sabry, Laura A. Favetta
pmc-13301040.description: Epigenetic regulation is pivotal in reproductive processes, such as oocyte maturation and pre-implantation embryonic development, and it impacts gene expression without altering DNA sequence through mechanisms including DNA methylation, histone modifications, and non-coding RNAs. Primarily, microRNA-21 is involved in meiotic progression, apoptosis, and cumulus cell function, which are necessary for oocyte competency.

pmc-13338035.title: Cell division and lineage dynamics during antheridium differentiation and male gametophyte development in Ceratopteris richardii
pmc-13338035.creator: Xi Yang, An Yan, Xing Liu, Yun Zhou
pmc-13338035.description: Sexual reproduction in land plants involves diverse strategies for gamete production and fertilization, significantly differing between seed plants, which deliver sperm via pollen, and seed-free plants such as ferns, which produce motile sperm within specialized multicellular structures, antheridia, on independently growing gametophytes.

pmc-13423760.title: A Multiagent Large Language Model Framework for Emergency Treatment Recommendation in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Development and Validation Study
pmc-13423760.creator: Bicong Yan, Ruipeng Zhang, Li Chen, Xinyu Song, Zhongzheng Cao, Yuehua Li, Ivan Steenstra
pmc-13423760.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAcute ischemic stroke (AIS) treatment selection requires rapid, guideline-concordant integration of clinical, imaging, and laboratory data, including therapeutic windows, contraindications, stroke severity, and imaging eligibility. This process is complex, expertise-dependent, and vulnerable to safety-critical errors.ObjectiveThis study aimed to develop and validate a structured multiagent large language model (LLM) framework for AIS decision support using real-world cases and to assess its accuracy, safety, auditability, and impact on physician decision-making, particularly among junior physicians and nonspecialists.MethodsWe developed a multiagent LLM framework that used structured

pmc-13632360.title: Enhancing patient care with AI agents: integrating advanced chatbot technologies for improved healthcare delivery
pmc-13632360.creator: Yasmine Abu Adla, Ahmad El Hajj
pmc-13632360.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare presents significant opportunities to enhance patient care and streamline medical workflows. However, challenges related to accuracy, reliability, and accessibility continue to limit the widespread adoption of AI-driven medical assistants. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to integrate multiple advanced AI techniques into a unified system designed to provide real-time, context-aware medical insights while ensuring accuracy, engagement, and interpretability.
